newsitem.title: INDIA: Incessant rain destroys south India rice crops.
newsitem.headline: Incessant rain destroys south India rice crops.

text.p: Rice crops worth millions of rupees have been destroyed by floods that ravaged coastal areas of India's southern state of Tamil Nadu since the beginning of December, police and officials said on Monday.

The standing rice crop in 108,034 hectares of the Cauvery delta, known as the rice bowl of Tamil Nadu, was completely destroyed by incessant rain during the last fortnight, state Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi, told reporters.

Four districts along the 500-km coastal strand were the worst affected, Karunanidhi said. They were Chengalpattu MGR, Villupuam Ramaswamy Padayachiyar, South Arcot Vallalar and Nagai district, all located south of the state capital Madras.
In the Cauvery delta alone, an estimated 175,000 tonnes of paddy crop were totally destroyed, S. Ranganathan, president of the Cauvery Delta Farmers' Welfare Association, told Reuters.
However, the floods had devastated only 25 percent of the area of the Cauvery delta although damage might be worse if the rainfall continued, he added.
"Fortunately 75 to 80 percent of the paddy crop is still unaffected in this delta -- but this situation will change radically if the rains continue beyond another day or two," Ranganathan said.
But weather officials said the skies over Madras were clear.
Karunanidhi said there was massive damage to property. He said 789 irrigation tanks had been breached, and 74 bridges and 1,855 km of roads had been damaged.
About 60,000 thatched huts were destroyed, Karunanidhi said. The state government had released 500 million rupees ($14 million) to feed the 600,000 people made homeless, he added.
In October, floods damaged 1.13 million hectares of fertile land, about eight percent of farmed areas in the neighbouring state of Andhra Pradesh.
